_comment: The one action catalog of ADR 004 D1. Plugin-owned and not user-editable: users set levels and per-action verdicts in permissions.json (core/schemas/permissions.schema.json), never here. Every id the D1 table names is here once; audit aliases fold into the canonical id. tests/test-permission-catalog.sh holds this file to the ADR (ids, R levels, machine tags, the unattended list, the D2 ceilings) and to every gh / git push / GraphQL / MCP call the skills and scripts make.

rubric.R1: Local: writes undone with git; nothing leaves the machine.
rubric.R2: Shared-additive: visible to others, additive or trivially revertible.
rubric.R3: Shared-mutating: changes shared state; undo is possible but costly or socially visible.
rubric.R4: Irreversible or privileged: cannot be undone, crosses a trust boundary, or changes permissions.
rules: Context may raise a level, never lower it (raises, denies).

tags.machine: D1 rubric gap: a local non-config effect outside the worktree. A mapping, not a sixth class: plugin-owned and session-scoped => R1; outside the worktree but owned and undoable by the plugin => R2; not owned, or code the user never chose => R3; persists into host config or trust, or forges a human signal => R4.

levels._comment: ADR 004 D2. A level is a ceiling over the plugin's own gates, never over the host.

verdicts.ask: Asks the human. No human present => deny, naming the setting that would allow it: the once-only --perms= route where D5 lists a host prompt, and the durable one (D6); for R4, that no setting allows it automatically.
verdicts.allow_if_precondition: allow iff the action has never_auto false and its unattended_precondition holds; otherwise ask. A precondition that cannot be established never holds.
verdicts.deny: Explicit deny from any layer, or a safety invariant (denies). Final at every level.

levels.r4: Ask on a host prompt (D5), per call, naming the id, the target and the effect, at every level. No ticket, file or env passes R4.

pr.merge.auto.widen: At standard, allow when actions["pr.merge.auto"] is "allow" in the user file or in a project file trusted per D3; otherwise ask (= auto-merge off).

conditions._comment: Named checks the resolver (D4) and the guard (PG) evaluate. A precondition holds only when established. A raise or deny applies when its condition holds OR cannot be established (D4: unknown never holds a precondition; SR S-12).
conditions.pinned_check_or_review_and_no_protected_: The base branch requires >= 1 status check with a pinned source (ruleset integration_id or classic app_id) or >= 1 approving review, and the PR diff touches nothing under .github/workflows/**, CODEOWNERS, .github/CODEOWNERS, docs/CODEOWNERS or .tamirs-superpowers/** (SR S-13).
conditions.pr_merged_not_default_not_cross_repo: The branch's PR is MERGED, the branch is neither the PR base nor the default branch, and the PR is not cross-repository.
conditions.own_pr_or_closes_ref_of_merged_pr: The PR was opened by this session's objective or task, or the issue is named by a Closes #N of a merged PR.
conditions.force_with_lease_and_own_claim: The push uses --force-with-lease (with an expected value) and the branch is claimed by this task (git.md: no force-push to base or to a branch another task works on).
conditions.pinned_lockfile: The install or exec resolves every package from a committed lockfile or an exact pinned version.
conditions.unmerged_no_remote_copy: The local branch holds commits that no remote ref and no merged PR contains.
conditions.unmerged_commits: The remote branch holds commits that the default branch does not contain and no merged PR carried.
conditions.drops_unpushed_commits: The operation makes commits unreachable that no remote ref contains.
conditions.discards_work: The operation discards uncommitted changes (tracked or untracked, not ignored) or commits that no remote ref contains.
conditions.uncommitted_changes: The working tree holds changes this task did not commit (safety invariant 4).
conditions.default_branch: The target branch is the repository's default branch (or cannot be shown not to be).
conditions.tag_ref: The ref is a tag (refs/tags/*, or a name that resolves to a tag with git show-ref --verify refs/tags/<name>).
conditions.workflow_hook_or_policy_path: A target path is under .github/workflows/**, .github/actions/**, CODEOWNERS, .github/CODEOWNERS, .tamirs-superpowers/**, .husky/** or .githooks/**, or, in this plugin's own repository, hooks/** or core/permissions/**.
conditions.others_thread: The review thread was started by someone else, or the agent has not replied to it.
conditions.protected_default_branch: The default branch is protected by a classic rule or a ruleset (safety invariant 5).
conditions.required_check_failing_or_pending: A required status check on the PR head is failing or pending (safety invariant 2).
conditions.push_remote_not_origin: The push goes to a remote, named or a URL, whose push URL is not one of origin's (an API branch write: to another repository than origin's). Local commits pushed anywhere but the repository the user cloned leave it (F9).

target_kinds._comment: D5: a ticket binds one target. Two targets are equal iff every listed field resolves on both sides and is equal; an unresolvable field never matches. Kind none has no target, so no ticket ever matches it: only the level ceiling can allow it.

matching._comment: How an equivalents entry matches a call (D1 Equivalents, SR S-07). PG implements exactly this; tests/test-permission-catalog.sh carries the reference matcher and its fixture table.
matching.result: A call maps to EVERY id with a matching entry. Its decision is the strictest of theirs (deny > ask > allow) and its reported id is the one with the highest r. A call with a mutation marker that maps to no id is UNCLASSIFIED.
matching.simple_commands: Split at ; && || | & and newlines, drop redirections and comments, and match each simple command alone. The commands of $(...), backticks, <(...), the string of sh -c / su -c / env -S / watch, a here-document or herestring fed to a shell, and find -exec are matched too. eval, make, interpreters and a script file's contents are the residual D1 names: the commands inside them are not seen. A construct PG's tokeniser cannot read the way a shell does (an unterminated quote or here-document, $'...', ((...)), case inside a substitution, nested backticks, nesting past 4 levels, a shell reading its script from a pipe) is UNCLASSIFIED.

prefix_value_options._comment: The options of a prefix command that take the next word as their value (that word is not the program). The program, a prefix command and a script are matched in any case: a case-insensitive file system runs GIT and PLUGIN-CONFIG.SH.

matching.env: Leading NAME=value words are env assignments. env_any globs match them; target_env names change the target, never the id.
matching.argv: cmd: the argv prefix after prefix commands, env assignments and the tool's global options; '*' matches one token. any / all / none: fnmatch globs over every token after argv[0] (after the script, for a script entry), global options and option values included; a glob that is a long option '--x' also matches '--x=<value>'. args / args_none: globs over the positional tokens after the cmd prefix (tokens not starting with '-' that are not the value of a value option); args_none ['*'] means no positional. first_arg_none: globs over the FIRST positional token only; the entry does not match when it matches one of them, and does match when there is no positional (a writer whose read-only subcommands are listed, every other form being a write). min_args: the entry matches only with at least that many positionals (git symbolic-ref <name> <ref> writes, git symbolic-ref <name> reads). env_any: globs over the leading assignments. gh's -R/--repo/--hostname (-Racme/app attached too) may stand anywhere and never count as cmd or positional tokens. argv[0] is matched in lower case (a case-insensitive file system runs GIT); a git config key glob (core.hooksPath, remote.*.url) in any case, as git reads it; a git long option written as a unique prefix (--no-verif, --har, --delet: git accepts it) is read as that option first. script: matches when argv[0], or ANY argument of an interpreter (bash, sh, zsh, ksh, dash, source, ., python*, node, ...) other than the value of one of its options (-o, -O, --rcfile, --init-file, -m, ...), equals the script path or ends with '/<script>', in any case, or is a glob a shell would expand to it; PG also follows links to, and byte-identical copies of, scripts/plugin-config.sh, setup.sh and install.sh, and reads any other command naming plugin-config.sh (cp, ln, mv, cat, ...) as policy.edit unless it only inspects it (F1).
matching.rest: method: an HTTP method or a list of them. gh api, its options read as pflag reads them (attached -ftag_name=v1, -XPOST, -f=k=v, --field=k=v, --input=f, separate, or in a cluster -iXPOST): -X/--method, else POST when -f/-F/--field/--raw-field/--input is given, else GET; every positional is a path (gh takes one). An HTTP client (http_clients) aimed at a github_api_hosts URL (the host in any case, with or without a scheme): curl -X/--request, else POST with -d/--data*/-F/--form/--json, PUT with -T/--upload-file — attached (-d'{..}', --data=..), separate or inside a short-option cluster (-sd ..), and --expand-<option> as <option> — unless -G/--get, else GET; wget --method (or -e method=), else POST with --post-data/--post-file/--body-data/--body-file (or -e post_data=), else GET; every github_api_hosts URL a curl or wget call is given (curl's --url too) is a path, under every method a curl --next group names; a path that maps to no id, and a call that reads URLs or options from a file (curl -K/--config, wget -i/--input-file, -e input=, a curl --expand-url {{variable}}), is UNCLASSIFIED beside the ids the others map to; http, https, xh and xhs (httpie syntax) take a method as their first positional, else POST with a data item (key=value, key:=json, key@file), else GET. A path drops scheme and host (and /api/v3 on GHE), a leading '/' and the query string, and matches its pattern in any case. In a pattern '{owner}/{repo}' matches two segments or one segment holding a shell expansion (a slug variable carries both); any other '{name}', and '*', match one segment; '**' matches the rest, including nothing; '{default}' is the target repository's default branch. fields_all / fields_none: globs over the key=value pairs of -f/-F/--field/--raw-field, or of a JSON body's top-level keys.
matching.graphql: gh api graphql, or a POST to a github_api_hosts /graphql: every mutation field the document names maps to the ids listing it. A document with no mutation is repo.read. A file-sourced document (-F query=@file, --field query=@file, --input) is UNCLASSIFIED.
matching.mcp: tool: the Claude-form tool name (see mcp). args_all / args_none: argument name to a glob over the argument's JSON value rendered as a string; args_all needs every listed argument to match, args_none needs none to.
matching.paths: Write-path rules (GSF, enforce-worktree-edits) are realpath globs: '{repo}' is the checkout root, '{home}' the passwd home (D3), '{plugin_root}' the running plugin root, '{worktree}' the task worktree.
matching.default_branch: '{default}' resolves to the target repository's default branch; when it cannot be resolved a pattern holding it matches (context may raise, never lower).
matching.target_remote: A git push whose remote is a URL or a path names its target directly; it is not origin.

unclassified.rule: A command that maps to no id but carries a mutation marker, or a file-sourced GraphQL query, is UNCLASSIFIED and treated as R4 (never automatic). An unknown action id given to the resolver is UNCLASSIFIED too.
unclassified._comment: D1 also names the gh token-printing subcommand and the two GitHub token variables as markers. They are kept as Python regular expressions searched anywhere in the command text (the same substring test as mutation_markers, nothing wider) so that no shipped file spells a credential name out: the plugin directory's scanner reads such a name as a credential read whatever the sentence says (scripts/check-claude-dist.sh).
unclassified.protected_path_marker: Any path a paths rule of policy.edit, workflow.edit or config.global.write names.
unclassified.residual: Wrappers (make, eval, $(...), xargs, a script the catalog does not name) and interpreters (python3 -c, node -e) are not seen through (ADR Open risks).

mcp._comment: Equivalents name tools in their Claude form. Strip claude_prefix for the bare tool name; OpenCode names the same tool github_<tool> (doc-cited); the Codex, Cursor and Gemini forms are unverified (D8). A tool of this server with no entry is UNCLASSIFIED.

host_bypass._comment: When Claude Code itself runs with bypassPermissions, permission-guard.sh steps aside for every ask except these: the operations that cannot be undone. The user's decision of 2026-11-06 (5.6.5): in bypass mode, ask only for something major and irreversible, such as deleting a remote repository or a major directory. Other hosts, denies and plugin-config confirms are unchanged.

actions.note: gh view/list and gh api GET. The gh subcommand that prints the stored token is not a read here: it is a D1 mutation marker (unclassified.mutation_marker_patterns).
Reading a secret-bearing config (capture-config, diagnose-refusal, session-report). Gated at L1 only.
Environment variable names, never values (diagnose-refusal).
Edits inside the task worktree. A path a stricter id names (workflow.edit, policy.edit, config.global.write) takes that id.
git commit with --no-verify, -n or a hooks override is also git.verify.skip (R4).
A rebase of an already-pushed branch needs git.push.force to publish.
A reset to a remote ref that discards nothing is a sync; one that discards work becomes git.reset_to_remote (R4).
Clean and pushed. --force on a clean, pushed worktree discards nothing; one that discards work becomes worktree.remove.force (R4).
Gitignored, regenerable directories only, behind cleanup.sh's check-ignore guard.
The host's own subagent tool. The child runs at the caller's ceiling, never higher. A nested agent-host process is process.spawn.agent_host (R4).
Plugin-owned, loopback, session-scoped (skill-creator eval viewer). L1 only.
A script of this worktree. A script from another repository is code.exec.foreign_repo (R3).
Own, non-default branch, to origin. Every git push, send-pack and http-push matches this id; the stricter push ids add to it, and a push to any other remote is raised to R3 (push_remote_not_origin).
Opening the PR and editing its text. Changing a PR's base is in no id: UNCLASSIFIED.
Re-runs an existing run. Dispatching a workflow (gh workflow run) is not a re-run: release.yml is release.create, anything else UNCLASSIFIED.
Threads the agent answered. Another person's thread is R3, never automatic (D1 R3 row).
A PR conversation comment is an issue comment on GitHub's API.

scripts/github-labels.sh apply: create and update the canonical label set on a repository (label.create + label.edit in one run, so one ask covers the sweep). Deleting a label it does not name is label.delete, asked separately and only with --prune.
Hands work to an agent with its own write access, which no level governs (ADR Open risks).
Non-default branch at R2; the default branch is R3, never automatic; workflows, hooks or policy are R4 (D1 R3 and R4 rows).
A write to a non-GitHub host. The same client aimed at a GitHub API host is matched by the rest entries of the GitHub ids.
A credential pasted into chat enters the transcript and the provider (notify-setup).
Plugin-owned daemon, PID verified.
Plugin-owned daemon, PID verified. Any other PID is process.kill (R3).
From the lockfile, in the own worktree, lifecycle scripts off. A hook never installs: it prints the command (SR S-08).
gh pr merge --auto only, so GitHub protection decides (D2). --delete-branch with --auto belongs to this id: GitHub deletes the head only once the merge lands.
A direct merge. The plugin never performs one automatically (D2).
GraphQL updatePullRequest can set state, so it maps here (context may raise, never lower).
Deleting a label strips it from every issue and PR that carried it, and GitHub keeps no history of which ones. github-labels.sh reaches it only with --prune typed.
GraphQL updateIssue can set state, so it maps here.
Own, non-default branch. GraphQL updateRef/updateRefs can force, so they map here.
The user's token can supply the required review. GraphQL review mutations can approve, so they map here.
Every repository-settings PATCH folds here, not only the merge settings the ADR names.
A write whose realpath is outside the worktree and that no stricter id (policy.edit, config.global.write) names. Path rule; no argv form.
A success status for a required context no app is pinned to satisfies the check (SR S-13).
An unverified or foreign PID. The plugin's own daemon by verified PID is daemon.stop (R2).
A model-named package from the network. With lifecycle scripts on it is also code.exec.foreign_repo.
Running a package fetched for the call (mcp-builder's inspector).
run, build, pull, up, prune. Replaces docker-guard.py's agent-typeable token with tickets (D5).
Code the user never chose: a foreign repository's script, and every install with lifecycle scripts on (incl. uv sync, bundle install). Never run by a hook.
Safety invariant 6: only the D5 host prompt grants the deliberate one-off.
--mirror can force-update and delete every ref, the default branch included.
Dispatching the release workflow publishes a release and a tag.
A bare refspec that names an existing tag is this id too (condition tag_ref).
Headless or not: a nested agent host delivers model text as a typed prompt and can answer a host prompt (D5).

Drives a terminal: can forge a typed prompt or answer a TTY or host prompt (D5), the guard's own R4 dialog included (implementation-measurements.md Impact 4). tmux: its global options (-L/-S/-f/... before the command, matching.global_options) are skipped, and the `any` entry catches what an exact argv prefix cannot: a unique-prefix abbreviation (send-k, pa, past), a clustered or attached option (-2u, -Lsock), a `\;`-chained command and a key-sending command quoted inside another (set-hook, run-shell). pipe-pane -I types a command's output into the pane. cmux: send, send-key, send-panel, send-key-panel, paste and paste-buffer after any global option, and an rpc method naming send or paste (inferred from the method names). wezterm cli send-text, kitty/kitten @ send-text|send-key, zellij action write|write-chars, iTerm's AppleScript `write text`, and the keystroke injectors ydotool, wtype and cliclick are the same verb. A wrapper script stays the D1 residual.
Includes forks. Excluded from the GitHub MCP server at every level (D8).
Apply, remove, and the legacy ensure-branch-protection.sh shim.
Local or remote. GSF denies locally and no deny text points at the MCP path any more (D10.5).

Global config, any git config that runs code (alias.*, core.hooksPath and friends), and the remote URLs and remote-tracking refs PG reads as facts: git remote add/set-url/rename/remove, an explicit git remote set-head (--auto asks the remote), git symbolic-ref/update-ref of refs/remotes/** and a fetch refspec into them, remote.*.url/pushurl and url.*.insteadOf (F9). They write {repo}/.git/config or the refs default_branch and the unpushed checks trust.
Adopted capture-config hunks land in platforms/*/settings.d and core/global-rules.md and may carry permission rules.

Permission files, lock, tickets, guard scripts, installed caches, host settings and option stores. Only the D6 writer writes them, through D5. Guard files in a source checkout are an R4 ask, not a deny (D10.1).
A worktree removal that discards uncommitted or unpushed work. Reached from worktree.remove (condition discards_work).
cleanup's explicit per-worktree drop, gitignored content included. L1 choice; the removal itself is worktree.remove raised by discards_work.
A reset to a remote ref that discards uncommitted or unpushed work. Reached from git.sync.ff (condition discards_work).

A recursive rm of a major directory: /, a top-level system directory, the home directory or one of its direct children, or a git repository's root. Matched in permission-guard.sh (rm_major_targets), not by an argv pattern, because it judges the resolved path. Added 2026-11-06 with host_bypass.
